findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:74 — `organization_context` is not defined in this method; any request with `optimized_pagination=true` will raise a `NameError`. The access check should be `request.user.is_superuser or request.member.has_global_access` (or via a permission class)

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:830-840 (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result) — negative start offset in QuerySet slicing (`list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`) raises Django `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so the negative-offset feature crashes instead of paginating and is non-functional

[High/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:139 — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` and crashes the consumer for messages from older producers without the new field; should use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise", <default>)` or a schema-version guard

[High/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:44-55 — switching from sets to sorted sets (`scard`→`zcard`, `sunionstore`→`zunionstore`) raises Redis `WRONGTYPE` on old `sadd`-written keys during rolling deploy, failing span processing for pre-existing buffered data; needs migration or type-tolerant path

[High/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61 — `zpopmin` silently drops oldest spans (lowest `end_timestamp_precise`) with no metric/log and can evict parent/segment spans, leaving orphaned children that cannot be materialized; unbounded silent data loss, whereas the Python flusher previously skipped oversized segments with a logged error

[Medium/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449-452 — removal of the `max_segment_spans` guard (`len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`) leaves no span-count backstop in the flush path if Lua eviction doesn't fire (pre-existing keys or `max_segment_spans` configured lower than 1000)

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — redirect-resolution loop limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with the explaining comment deleted; segment trees deeper than 1000 fail to resolve to the root, so spans attach to a non-root set and the tree is never joined correctly — a regression for deep traces

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-186 — the `start_offset = max(0, offset)` change in the base `BasePaginator.get_result` silently changes behavior for all existing paginators, making negative-offset cursors return results starting at offset 0 and masking malformed cursors; if intended only for the new paginator it should live in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`

[Medium/security] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:69-86 — user-controlled `optimized_pagination` query parameter switches to a paginator granting access beyond normal pagination bounds, gated only by `has_global_access` (which does not imply superuser); should be a server-side/feature-flag decision, and the queryset-level permissions claim is asserted but not enforced in this diff

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — missing tests for (a) `OptimizedCursorPaginator` including negative-offset behavior, (b) the >1000-span eviction path in the Lua script, (c) WRONGTYPE/back-compat with pre-existing set keys, and (d) consumer behavior when `end_timestamp_precise` is missing from the payload

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — the removed comment documented the known failure mode of the depth limit; deleting it rather than updating it for the new limit loses the only documentation of this edge case

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

If it is not defined elsewhere earlier in the method/file, this would raise a `NameError` before pagination logic runs (note: it would happen regardless of `optimized_pagination=true` since `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:139 — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` and crashes the consumer for messages from older producers without the new field; should use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise", <default>)` or a schema-version guard

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the new field is accessed as `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` when constructing `Span`. Since `val` comes from `rapidjson.loads(payload.value)` and there is no guard/default, any message payload that lacks this key will raise `KeyError` and crash batch processing. The diff shows this key was newly introduced (tests were updated to include it), but no backward-compat handling was added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:44-55 — switching from sets to sorted sets (`scard`→`zcard`, `sunionstore`→`zunionstore`) raises Redis `WRONGTYPE` on old `sadd`-written keys during rolling deploy, failing span processing for pre-existing buffered data; needs migration or type-tolerant path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure for the same keys (e.g. `span-buf:s:{...}:<id>`) from Sets to Sorted Sets: Python now writes with `zadd` (was `sadd`) and reads with `zscan` (was `sscan`), and the Lua script switches `scard`→`zcard` and `sunionstore`→`zunionstore`. There is no type-tolerant logic or migration/dual-read path for pre-existing keys that were already created as Sets by the old code. During a rolling deploy or immediately after upgrade with buffered data still present, calling `zcard/zunionstore/zscan` on a Set key will raise Redis `WRONGTYPE`, breaking span processing until those keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:59-61 — `zpopmin` silently drops oldest spans (lowest `end_timestamp_precise`) with no metric/log and can evict parent/segment spans, leaving orphaned children that cannot be materialized; unbounded silent data loss, whereas the Python flusher previously skipped oversized segments with a logged error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds hard trimming in `add-buffer.lua`: when `span_count > 1000`, it executes `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which irreversibly deletes the lowest-scored members (with `zadd` using `span.end_timestamp_precise` as the score per `buffer.py`). This is silent (no metric/log in the Lua script) and can drop any spans in the set, including spans that are structurally important (e.g., parents/segment roots) since there is no protection by type—potentially leaving children without their parents when later materializing. The previous Python path explicitly logged/metric’d and skipped oversized segments; that safeguard is removed and replaced by eviction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449-452 — removal of the `max_segment_spans` guard (`len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`) leaves no span-count backstop in the flush path if Lua eviction doesn't fire (pre-existing keys or `max_segment_spans` configured lower than 1000)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Python-side span-count safeguard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` (the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` check is deleted) and does not add an equivalent enforcement in the flush path. While `add-buffer.lua` now prunes ZSETs to 1000 members via `zpopmin`, the Python writer path in `process_spans` was changed to `p.zadd(...)` with no cap, so a segment key can grow beyond any configured `max_segment_spans` (or beyond 1000 if Lua pruning isn’t invoked for that key). This is a correctness/operational regression: the configured count limit is no longer guaranteed during flush.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — redirect-resolution loop limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with the explaining comment deleted; segment trees deeper than 1000 fail to resolve to the root, so spans attach to a non-root set and the tree is never joined correctly — a regression for deep traces

adjudication.rationale: The diff in add-buffer.lua changes the redirect-resolution loop from `for i = 0, 10000 do -- ...depth 10k...` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes the explanatory comment. The loop is the only mechanism shown for following the redirect chain (`hget` in a loop with `break` on termination), and there is no fallback/error handling if the chain exceeds the iteration cap. If a redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the loop will terminate without reaching the ultimate/root `set_span_id`, and the script will proceed to `hset`/merge using a non-root `set_span_id`, matching the described “tree never joined correctly” failure mode. This is a behavior regression for sufficiently deep chains introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-186 — the `start_offset = max(0, offset)` change in the base `BasePaginator.get_result` silently changes behavior for all existing paginators, making negative-offset cursors return results starting at offset 0 and masking malformed cursors; if intended only for the new paginator it should live in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the core pagination slice in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` from `queryset[offset:stop]` to using `start_offset = max(0, offset)` when `not cursor.is_prev` (lines ~176-186). This clamps any negative `cursor.offset` to 0 instead of letting the ORM/QuerySet raise on negative slicing, which silently alters behavior for all existing paginators using this base implementation and can mask malformed/forged cursors by returning the first page rather than erroring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:69-86 — user-controlled `optimized_pagination` query parameter switches to a paginator granting access beyond normal pagination bounds, gated only by `has_global_access` (which does not imply superuser); should be a server-side/feature-flag decision, and the queryset-level permissions claim is asserted but not enforced in this diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a user-controlled switch `optimized_pagination=true` in `organization_auditlogs.py` that selects a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and passes `enable_advanced_features=True` when `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` (lines 69-86). The new paginator contains an “advanced feature” branch that explicitly allows negative offsets (`if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0: start_offset = cursor.offset`) and justifies it via comments about queryset-level permission checks, but no such enforcement exists in the paginator itself. However, the finding’s claim that this “grants access beyond normal pagination bounds” as a security issue isn’t directly verifiable as an authorization bypass from the diff alone (the endpoint queryset is still organization-scoped), making this more of an architectural/security-hardening review concern than a concrete proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — missing tests for (a) `OptimizedCursorPaginator` including negative-offset behavior, (b) the >1000-span eviction path in the Lua script, (c) WRONGTYPE/back-compat with pre-existing set keys, and (d) consumer behavior when `end_timestamp_precise` is missing from the payload

adjudication.rationale: The finding is framed as a test gap, but the diff shows real backward-compat/runtime break risks: (c) span buffer Redis keys previously written as SETs via `sadd`/`sscan` now are treated as ZSETs via `zadd`/`zscan` using the same key pattern (`span-buf:s:{...}:...`), which will cause Redis WRONGTYPE errors for any pre-existing keys until they expire; no conversion/guard exists. (d) the consumer now unconditionally reads `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` when building `Span`, so older/malformed payloads lacking that field will raise a KeyError and break processing. These are verifiable defects introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — the removed comment documented the known failure mode of the depth limit; deleting it rather than updating it for the new limit loses the only documentation of this edge case

adjudication.rationale: In add-buffer.lua the loop bound was changed from `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with the explanatory comment removed. This does remove the only inline documentation of the known failure mode/edge case tied to the depth limit, and the diff does not add replacement documentation elsewhere.
